response_text: This study develops a machine‑learning model to predict whether water is safe to drink. Using data from diverse sources, the authors measured standard water‑quality parameters—pH, turbidity, total dissolved solids (TDS), conductivity, hardness, and others—and trained several binary classifiers (logistic regression, random forests, XGBoost, and SVM). The support‑vector‑machine model achieved the best performance, correctly classifying 82.3 % of samples. Feature importance analysis identified pH, TDS, and hardness as the most influential predictors of potability. The resulting model can inform water‑quality decisions and, due to its scalability, can be deployed online for real‑time assessment by users. Overall, the work demonstrates that supervised learning can effectively support public health by improving access to safe drinking water.
